title: ##混沌动态网络优化算法 (CDNO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, the混沌动态网络优化 (CDNO) algorithm, designed to address the challenges of complex dynamic network optimization, particularly in scenarios involving traffic flow and resource allocation. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with rapidly changing environments, necessitating more adaptable and efficient solutions. CDNO leverages dynamic chaos theory to achieve optimized solutions through a combination of adaptive control, dynamic network modeling, and iterative refinement. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a dynamic chaos model, allowing the algorithm to respond effectively to evolving network conditions. This paper details the algorithm's design, its key components, and its demonstrated performance on a variety of dynamic network optimization problems. We highlight the advantages of CDNO compared to existing methods, emphasizing its ability to handle complex, non-linear dynamics. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the application of this algorithm to further enhance optimization capabilities in dynamic network systems.

title: 基于自适应网络的强化学习算法的优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm based on adaptive neural networks designed for optimizing complex control systems. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on manually defined reward functions, which can be difficult to design and may not capture the true desired behavior of the system. Our proposed algorithm leverages adaptive neural networks to automatically adjust control strategies, resulting in more effective control compared to traditional methods. We present a framework that allows the network to learn optimal control policies through self-adaptation, addressing the limitations of manual reward engineering. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted network structure that continuously learns and refines its parameters based on feedback, enabling more robust and adaptable control. The work explores the impact of network architecture and training techniques on the performance of the optimized control system.

title: Quantum Entanglement Simulation: A Quantum Information Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, offers a unique platform for simulating complex quantum systems. Traditional computational methods struggle to effectively handle these intricate systems, often requiring exponentially increasing computational resources. This paper introduces a novel quantum information adaptive algorithm based on the principles of quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the fragility of entanglement to dynamically adjust simulation parameters based on the outcome of the simulation, thereby enabling automated parameterization and optimization, significantly reducing computational cost. We present a detailed explanation of the core mechanism, including the mathematical formulation of the entanglement-based feedback loop and its impact on the simulation process. This research explores the potential of this approach to revolutionize quantum simulation, offering a pathway towards more efficient and adaptable simulations of complex quantum systems.

title: Title: Geometric Proof Systems Based on Self-Referential Constraints
abstract: This paper introduces a novel class of proof systems predicated on self-referential constraints within geometric proofs. The core concept is to develop a mechanism whereby the system learns to generate constraints that are intrinsically linked to its own properties, fostering automated verification of complex mathematical structures. This system aims to revolutionize the verification process in geometry and related fields, moving beyond manual intervention and leveraging a fundamentally intelligent approach. The proposed system offers a significant advancement in proof verification through recursive analysis, establishing a new paradigm for automated mathematical validation.

title: Dynamics of Metarepresentation and Structural Limits of Self Containment: A Diagonalization and Transfinite Cardinal Approach
abstract: We formalize the problem of epistemic self-containment in reflective agents usingstate-space representation and operator theory. By defining a metarepresentation operator Φover a family of cognitive frontiers F ⊆ P(U), we demonstrate that complete self-containmentis strictly impossible for any internal representation framework. Utilizing a Tarski-Cantor diag-onal argument, we prove that no finite internal frame can contain its own evaluation predicate,forcing a strictly ascending chain of representation frontiers F0 ⊊ F1 ⊊ F2 . . . . Furthermore, byanalyzing exhaustive metarepresentation through power-set dynamics, we map this expansionto the transfinite hierarchy of Beth numbers (ℶn). We conclude that the reflexive zero-pointlimit Fω is structurally inaccessible in finite steps, establishing a general barrier theorem forself-modeling systems with applications to recursive AI self-improvement, logical proof barriers,and physical observer bounds.

title: A Quantum Computing Method for AC Power Flow with Residual-Controlled Dynamic Precision
abstract: To address the amplification of correction errors caused by an ill-conditioned AC power-flow Jacobian under heavily loaded operating conditions, as well as the excessive circuit depth associated with a fixed quantum-solution accuracy, this paper proposes a residual-controlled, regularized quantum singular-value transformation (QSVT) method within an inexact Newton power-flow framework. First, the power-mismatch vector and state variables are scaled, and the Newton correction is reformulated as a Tikhonov-regularized least-squares subproblem. A bounded regularization filter is then approximated using Chebyshev polynomials, allowing QSVT to directly transform the singular values of the Jacobian matrix. On this basis, the residual of the linear subproblem associated with the quantum-approximate correction is defined, and constraints are established to relate the polynomial-approximation error, block-encoding error, and quantum measurement error to the inexact Newton forcing term. The QSVT polynomial degree and quantum-solution accuracy are subsequently adjusted dynamically according to the outer power-flow residual. Theoretical analysis establishes the boundedness of the regularized correction, a sufficient descent condition for the quantum-approximate correction, and the relationship between the solution error and cumulative query complexity under dynamically controlled quantum accuracy.

title: Topology-Aware Training and Spatial Diagnostics for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology
abstract: Anatomic tracer studies reveal how axon bundles project from an injection site, branch into smaller groups of axons, and course through the brain to reach their destinations. Histological data from such studies provide anatomical reference information for validating diffusion MRI tractography. However, manual annotation of the histological data is very labor-intensive, and although automated segmentation methods have been proposed, they rely mainly on pixel-overlap losses such as BCE and Dice; topology-aware loss functions have not been studied for this task. We compare BCE-Dice, clDice, Betti matching, and Topograph for fiber bundle segmentation in macaque tracer histology using a frozen DINOv3 backbone. To our knowledge, this is the first exploration of foundation-model features for this task. BCE-Dice achieved the highest Dice, while clDice achieved the highest bundle recall but poor mask overlap. Topograph had similar Dice to BCE-Dice, the lowest $β_0$ error, and fewer false positives than BCE-Dice and Betti matching. Fiber bundle segmentation methods are typically evaluated with a permissive rule that counts a bundle as detected given any overlap with the prediction. We show this rule does not capture oversegmentation, and that per-section TPR can be inflated by empty sections assigned perfect recall. To quantify this, we introduce Excess32, a spatial diagnostic measuring predicted pixels outside a 32-pixel tolerance band around annotated bundles. In validation, a Betti-Topograph union raises sparse-bundle TPR from 0.818 to 0.933, but worsens FDR from 0.296 to 0.509, Excess32 from 0.108 to 0.466, and area ratio from 0.94 to 3.34. These results show detection metrics alone are insufficient to characterize segmentation quality.

title: A Non-Formulable Theorem: A Fundamental Limit of Finite Syntactic Systems and Its Consequences for Security and AI
abstract: For every coherent and sufficiently expressive finite syntactic system S, we prove the existence of at least one theorem that S cannot produce autonomously. The result is a metatheorem: it proves the existence of a theorem, and applies to every finite syntactic system - security mechanisms, AI systems, formal verifiers, legal systems, economic models, and the formal system in which it is itself proved.

title: Quantum Hamiltonian Evolution for Coherent Quantum Learning
abstract: We introduce Coherent Quantum Learning (CQL), a training framework for quantum learning models in which the model parameters are quantum degrees of freedom evolved under a Hamiltonian that encodes the loss function. Current quantum machine learning retains classical optimization: parameters are updated by a classical outer loop using gradient estimates from measurements, and quantum coherence has no role in the training dynamics, just as in any classical treatment of the same problem. In the quantum case, a parameter register initialized in superposition evolves unitarily, and probability amplitude concentrates near low-loss configurations through interference, without gradient computation or classical feedback. We give an explicit construction using block encodings and Hamiltonian simulation, applicable to arbitrary parameterized circuits. Numerical experiments on binary classification and interferometric phase estimation confirm that the evolved distribution peaks at the optimal parameters, matching gradient-based performance. The construction is compatible in principle with fault-tolerant implementations and extends to batched training via sequential Hamiltonian evolution.

title: An Adversarial Zero-Shot Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate IoT Traffic Data
abstract: Anomaly detection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks presents unique challenges due to the diversity of devices, lack of labeled data, and domain variability across environments. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection that leverages adversarial learning and contrastive loss within a sequence-based Variational Autoencoder (VAE) architecture. Our method enables zero-shot domain adaptation by jointly optimizing domain-invariant latent representations and semantically structured embedding spaces, without requiring labeled data or raw feature transfer. To address the heterogeneity of IoT deployments, we introduce encoder and decoder adaptor layers that align feature distributions across domains while preserving contextual semantics. Additionally, we propose a destination-based segmentation strategy to better model real-world communication structures in IoT traffic. Our framework is comprehensively evaluated on six distinct datasets spanning industrial, enterprise, general-purpose, smart home, and military automation domains across 44 transfer scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate strong zero-shot generalization in several cross-domain settings and competitive performance against a contrastive domain-adaptation baseline under realistic, heterogeneous, and privacy-constrained IoT conditions.

title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories
abstract: We study the override and update operators on partial functions from the perspective of restriction categories. We propose a definition of override restriction categories, in which both of the operators in question exist. We prove a number of results concerning these operators and their relationship to the structure of the ambient restriction category, as well as relating them to the existing literature on the override and update operators. We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非线性优化算法
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for optimization algorithms, specifically targeting complex optimization problems with non-linear constraints. We propose a novel non-linear optimization algorithm predicated on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance the exploration of the solution space and facilitate the discovery of global optima. The core mechanism revolves around leveraging entanglement to induce non-linearity within the optimization process, thereby enabling the algorithm to navigate complex landscapes more effectively than classical methods. This work explores the theoretical underpinnings and potential practical applications of this approach, highlighting its novelty through the design of a fundamentally new modeling methodology. The paper details the proposed algorithm's structure, analysis of its performance characteristics, and initial experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in challenging optimization scenarios.

title: Algorithmic Bias Mitigation via Differential Privacy (ABPD)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Bias Mitigation via Differential Privacy (ABPD), a novel approach to mitigating bias in machine learning models. Traditional bias mitigation techniques often involve post-processing or targeted data modifications, which can be computationally expensive and may not fully address the root cause of bias. ABPD leverages differential privacy, a rigorous privacy mechanism, to add controlled noise to the model parameters during training, effectively protecting against sensitive information while still allowing the model to learn effectively. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABPD through a series of experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing a significant reduction in bias across multiple metrics. The core of the method involves a carefully crafted noise addition process that maintains model accuracy while minimizing the impact of sensitive data.

title: Dimension Reduction Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel dimension reduction theory based on the Gaussian process framework, designed to effectively reduce high-dimensional data while maximizing information retention. The core concept revolves around leveraging the power of Gaussian processes to achieve this goal, offering a robust and adaptable approach compared to traditional dimensionality reduction methods. We introduce a method that systematically refines the Gaussian process to identify and eliminate irrelevant components, resulting in a lower-dimensional representation that preserves the crucial information present in the original dataset. The resulting data is presented with a focus on its statistical properties and the resulting reduced dimensionality. The paper demonstrates the efficacy of this technique through a series of numerical experiments and analyzes its impact on various datasets, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Simulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new perspective on geometric simulations, promising enhanced precision and the ability to model complex phenomena previously inaccessible to classical approaches. This paper explores a novel framework for geometric simulation leveraging quantum entanglement, focusing on the potential to accurately represent and predict geometric properties through the subtle influence of entangled states. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts geometric transformations based on entangled correlations, aiming to bridge the gap between classical geometry and quantum mechanics. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods by incorporating a non-linear geometric process driven by quantum entanglement. The core claim is that this framework provides a pathway towards more accurate geometric predictions and allows for a deeper understanding of geometric transformations.

title: Title: Topological拓扑拓扑 Framework for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly advancing field with immense potential to revolutionize various industries. However, current quantum computing architectures face significant challenges, primarily related to the need for complex control and optimization. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing framework based on topological topology, specifically leveraging self-similarity to enhance computational efficiency and control. The framework provides a robust and adaptable approach to quantum algorithm design and optimization, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing self-similarity to achieve improved performance and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The goal is to build a quantum computing paradigm that is both highly efficient and resilient to noise.

title: 基于图的量子态计算与优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational and optimization framework based on graph representations of quantum states. Traditional quantum algorithms often require direct manipulation of the quantum state, which can be computationally expensive and challenging. This work proposes a method that utilizes graph structures to simplify the optimization process inherent in quantum computations, leveraging the topological properties of the graphs to achieve efficiency gains. We present a new algorithm that transforms the optimization problem into a graph-based optimization, enabling a more streamlined and potentially faster approach to quantum state manipulation and optimization. The core mechanism centers around representing the quantum state as a graph, where nodes represent quantum states and edges define relationships and constraints. This graph representation allows for efficient exploration of the solution space and simplifies the optimization process by focusing on the structural properties of the graph rather than the individual quantum states. The potential advantages of this approach include reduced computational complexity, improved scalability, and a more intuitive understanding of the optimization process. We provide a theoretical analysis and initial implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in a specific quantum algorithm.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应量子电路设计
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for scientific and technological advancements. However, scaling and maintaining the fidelity of quantum circuits presents significant challenges. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit design based on the principles of quantum topology, specifically utilizing the concept of topologically protected quantum states. We propose a self-adaptive circuit design methodology that automatically adjusts circuit parameters to optimize performance and efficiency. The core mechanism revolves around leveraging the inherent robustness of topological structures in quantum systems to achieve precise control and manipulation of quantum states. This method offers a significant improvement over conventional methods by automating the optimization process and enhancing the overall reliability of quantum circuits. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and present preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving targeted circuit improvements. The impact of this design on quantum computation efficiency is expected to be substantial.

However, scaling and maintaining the fidelity of quantum circuits presents significant challenges. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit design based on the principles of quantum topology, specifically utilizing the concept of topologically protected quantum states. We propose a self-adaptive circuit design methodology that automatically adjusts circuit parameters to optimize performance and efficiency. The core mechanism revolves around leveraging the inherent robustness of topological structures in quantum systems to achieve precise control and manipulation of quantum states. This method offers a significant improvement over conventional methods by automating the optimization process and enhancing the overall reliability of quantum circuits. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and present preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving targeted circuit improvements. The impact of this design on quantum computation efficiency is expected to be substantial.

title: Dynamic Probability Space Optimization
abstract: Dynamic probability space optimization aims to create and optimize a system's internal structure dynamically, adapting to changes in data. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging self-adaptive optimization algorithms to form a dynamic probability space. The core mechanism involves systematically adjusting the structure of the probability space based on observed data, ensuring stability and resilience to evolving data patterns. This offers a significant advancement over traditional static optimization methods, providing a robust solution for systems requiring continuous adaptation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Field Resonance
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement field resonance to achieve precise control and measurement of entangled states, with the ultimate goal of revolutionizing quantum computation and information security. The core claim is the design of a quantum field capable of dynamically adjusting its frequency to precisely influence the evolution of entangled states, enabling highly accurate state detection and serving as a foundational element for quantum key distribution. The proposed method avoids the limitations of traditional measurement techniques by leveraging the inherent properties of the quantum field itself.

title: Neuroevolution of Adaptive Neurons
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design utilizing neuroevolution, specifically focusing on the adaptive design of individual neurons. The core concept involves employing an evolutionary algorithm to autonomously optimize the structural parameters of neurons, leading to the creation of highly specialized and energy-efficient neurons. Unlike traditional training methods that primarily adjust synaptic weights, this research directly manipulates neuron morphology – parameters such as synaptic connection weights, axon length, and dendrite size. The evolutionary process iteratively refines these parameters based on the neuron's performance within a defined task, utilizing a fitness function that quantifies this performance. The resulting adaptive neurons demonstrate a significant potential for improved efficiency and specialization compared to conventionally designed networks. The core algorithm is described in detail, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The method's capacity to create networks with bespoke neuron architectures tailored to specific tasks is explored. Finally, the potential for scaling this approach to larger and more complex neural networks is discussed.

title: ##基于量子纠错码的分布式存储系统设计
abstract: This paper proposes a design for a fault-tolerant distributed storage system leveraging quantum error-correcting codes. The core claim centers on using these codes to significantly enhance the reliability of data storage in a distributed environment. The proposed system employs quantum error-correcting codes for both encoding and decoding, effectively mitigating data corruption and ensuring data integrity. The novelty lies in the direct application of quantum error correction within a distributed storage architecture, addressing the inherent vulnerabilities of traditional storage systems to quantum decoherence and errors. This design offers a pathway towards robust data preservation in quantum computing scenarios. The system utilizes a layered approach, combining classical network infrastructure with quantum error correction protocols to achieve optimal performance. Key performance metrics such as error correction rate, storage overhead, and network latency are analyzed. The system's architecture is scalable and adaptable to varying storage requirements.

title: Dynamic Concept Graph Semantic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for dynamic concept graph semantic reasoning. The core idea is to construct a concept graph that can continuously update and evolve, and to leverage graph reasoning techniques for enhanced semantic understanding and knowledge discovery. The framework employs a dynamic graph structure based on knowledge graphs, integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to facilitate concept association learning and inference. Unlike static knowledge graphs, this approach addresses the inherent dynamism of knowledge by incorporating mechanisms for real-time adaptation and evolution. This results in a more accurate and timely understanding of complex semantic relationships. The system utilizes a series of algorithms to identify relevant concepts, establish connections, and perform reasoning based on the evolving graph structure. The key contribution lies in the combination of dynamic graph modeling with robust reasoning capabilities, enabling a more adaptive and intelligent semantic understanding system. The framework's performance is evaluated through simulated scenarios, demonstrating its ability to capture and reason about changing information effectively.

title: Quantum Information Theory via Integrated Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the application of integrated geometry to formalize the principles of quantum information theory. We propose a novel model where quantum states are represented as points within a higher-dimensional space, and the evolution of these points is governed by complex differential equations. The core mechanism involves the development of a "Quantum Geometry" algorithm that automatically generates and analyzes quantum circuits based on geometric structures. This approach aims to move beyond a purely statistical view of quantum mechanics, establishing a geometric framework for understanding and manipulating quantum information.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Modeling Complex Social Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling complex social systems utilizing Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks often struggle to accurately represent the intricate, nested relationships and feedback loops inherent in social dynamics. This work argues that a hierarchical structure is essential for effectively capturing these complexities. The proposed framework allows for modeling social systems at multiple levels of abstraction, facilitating the analysis of social processes and prediction of behavior. The core mechanism involves constructing an HBN with interconnected Bayesian networks at different levels, where higher-level networks represent overarching social structures and lower-level networks detail specific interactions. The resulting model offers improved representational power and analytical capabilities compared to traditional Bayesian Network approaches. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology through a conceptual framework and outline key considerations for its implementation, highlighting the benefits of integrating multiple levels of analysis within a unified probabilistic framework. The model incorporates key elements such as agent interactions, social norms, and influence networks, allowing for a more nuanced understanding of social phenomena. Finally, we discuss the potential for future research and development in this area, including the application of HBNs to real-world social systems.

title: 基于动态的自适应的图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive graph neural network (DSAN) architecture designed to enhance the performance of graph neural networks. Traditional graph neural networks often rely on static graph structures, limiting their adaptability and potential for improvement. This work proposes a dynamic self-adaptive approach where the network structure is continuously adjusted based on the input data, leading to improved feature representation and model generalization. We present a novel mechanism for dynamic graph structure adjustment, incorporating a feedback loop to maintain optimal graph topology. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in various performance metrics, including accuracy, robustness, and generalization ability. The proposed DSAN architecture offers a promising approach to overcome the limitations of static graph networks and achieve superior performance across diverse graph datasets.

The core mechanism involves an iterative adjustment process driven by a feedback loop, continuously refining the network's structure to maximize accuracy and generalization. This work introduces a unique dynamic parameter adjustment strategy that distinguishes itself from existing approaches, promising improved robustness and adaptability within a wide range of applications.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络的梯度调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel gradient adjustment algorithm based on adaptive neural networks, designed to enhance model stability and accuracy by dynamically adjusting gradient magnitudes during training. The proposed method addresses a significant limitation of existing gradient adjustment techniques, which often rely on fixed, static adjustments. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a "self-adaptive adjustment" mechanism that continuously monitors and adjusts the gradient based on the inherent noise and uncertainty within the learning process. The algorithm incorporates a mechanism to dynamically modulate gradient magnitude, leading to improved convergence, reduced sensitivity to initialization, and enhanced generalization performance. We present a series of experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach across a diverse range of neural network architectures and datasets. The results demonstrate that this adaptive gradient adjustment significantly outperforms traditional gradient descent methods in terms of training speed and model robustness.

title: Title: Quantum Error Mitigation using Entangled Probe Networks
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements, but inherent fragility necessitates robust error mitigation techniques. Traditional methods often involve full error correction, which is computationally expensive and requires significant resources. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing entangled probe networks to effectively mitigate errors without demanding full error correction. We investigate the design and implementation of such a network, demonstrating its potential to significantly reduce error rates in quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around strategically placing entangled probes to create a 'noisy-but-robust' environment, averaging out errors through correlated measurements. This approach offers a promising alternative to existing methods, potentially simplifying quantum computations while maintaining high accuracy.

title: Technologies quantiques pour l’énergie
abstract: Le document présente la stratégie d’EDF R&D autour des technologies quantiques appliquées à l’énergie. Face aux limites futures du calcul haute performance (HPC), notamment en complexité, coûts et consommation, le calcul quantique est envisagé à EDF R&D comme une perspective permettant d’aborder des problèmes aujourd’hui inaccessibles. Les cas d’usage couvrent toute la chaîne de valeur du système électrique : optimisation des réseaux et de la production, sûreté nucléaire via les études probabilistes, modélisation physique (équations aux dérivées partielles) et vieillissement des matériaux. L’entreprise s’appuie sur de nombreux partenariats industriels et académiques pour co-développer des algorithmes solutions. Des applications connexes, comme les capteurs quantiques pour la détection de défauts, sont également explorées. En conclusion, le quantique constitue un levier stratégique complémentaire pour anticiper les ruptures technologiques, et renforcer la performance du système électrique.

title: Beyond Transparency: Reframing Ethical Explainability in Human–AI Teams
abstract: Purpose: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly promoted as a mechanism for improving transparency, trust, and accountability in AI-assisted decision-making. However, its ethical value remains uncertain when AI systems are embedded within human teams and organizational workflows. This systematic literature review examines ethical issues associated with XAI in human–AI team contexts and explores how trust, decision-making, and accountability are associated with the use of XAI systems across organizational domains. Methodology: Guided by the SALSA framework and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review synthesized 25 studies drawn from healthcare, business and finance, cyber–physical systems, Earth Observation, and broader human–AI collaboration contexts. Findings: The findings revealed four interrelated themes: the paradox of explainability, in which transparency does not necessarily produce understanding; trust as a dynamic and fragile process shaped by user expertise, task stakes, and workflow integration; distributed accountability and the unresolved ethics of responsibility in human–AI collaboration; and bias, fairness, and the limits of explainability as a standalone ethical solution. Across the reviewed literature, XAI did not function as a self-sufficient safeguard against ethical risk. Rather, its ethical value depended on how explanations were designed, interpreted, coordinated within teams, and governed by organizations. Based on these findings, the study proposes the Sociotechnical Explainability Alignment (SEA) framework, which conceptualizes ethical XAI as requiring alignment across four levels: design, user, team, and organization. The review contributes to XAI scholarship by reframing explainability as a sociotechnical capability rather than a purely technical feature. It also offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to implement AI systems responsibly through human-centered design, trust calibration, role-sensitive explanation practices, and governance mechanisms that support accountability and fairness.

title: Characterization of the Implementation of Solar Photovoltaic Systems for Sustainable Urban Energy Planning in the Urban Area of Cuenca, Ecuador
abstract: This study characterizes the photovoltaic potential of three urban areas in Cuenca, Ecuador, located in the San Sebastián, Totoracocha, and Yanuncay parishes, through twelve technical, energy-related, socioeconomic, and environmental indicators. The analysis was complemented with grid simulations in CYME 9.2 to assess photovoltaic integration capacity in the distribution network and with a multicriteria synthesis using PROMETHEE II. The variables considered included solar irradiation, usable rooftop area, electricity consumption, population density, socioeconomic level, and the operating characteristics of distribution transformers. The results show that photovoltaic potential varies according to urban morphology, electricity demand, and the operating capacity of the grid. Totoracocha exhibited the highest theoretical potential and a self-sufficiency level of 99.1%, but it also recorded the lowest technical utilization factor, at 15.6%, because of transformer constraints. Yanuncay achieved the highest estimated technically available surplus under the evaluated operating scenarios, at 452,737 kWh/year, whereas San Sebastián exhibited the highest technical utilization factor, at 27.2%. The simulations confirmed that transformers constitute the main technical constraint on photovoltaic integration, while medium-voltage lines and voltage levels remained within their operating limits. The technically usable surplus energy could be allocated to induction cooking, electric mobility, or green hydrogen production as alternative, non-simultaneous scenarios. The energy allocated to self-sufficiency could avoid approximately 1022.5 tCO2/year. Orientation analysis showed statistically significant but limited differences among the evaluated configurations, indicating that orientation should be considered together with other rooftop and grid-related factors rather than as a standalone feasibility criterion. Overall, the proposed integrated framework provides a comparative decision-support basis for sustainable urban photovoltaic planning by jointly considering rooftop potential, electricity demand, grid constraints, socioeconomic conditions, and environmental benefits.

title: Seeing Through the Noise: Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Adversarially Robust Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Although the Deep Learning (DL) models have been crucial in the modern-day Artificial Intelligence (AI) appliances, its susceptibility to adversarial attacks remains critical. This is mainly critical in mission-critical systems and applications like autonomous vehicles. Although most of the current defense techniques aim to enhance the classification accuracy under attacks, but they often fail to address the fundamental damage to the visual input itself. In this literature, the authors put forward an adversarial defense architectural framework that improves the robustness by reconstructing the clean images from adversarially perturbed inputs, rather than optimizing the classification operations. This architectural framework utilizes a Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) paradigm to train an autoencoder fitted with the skip connection and multi-head attention mechanisms. This allows the architectural framework to restore perceptually and structurally genuine representations of the actual scenes. Here, the authors assessed the approach utilizing the CCF BDCI Traffic Light Detection dataset under the influences of FGSM and PGD attacks, analyzing the quality of the reconstruction by MSE, PSNR, and SSIM. The results show that this architectural framework can reconstruct the critical visual information from the adversarially attacked images, providing a foundational level of defense that enables the perceptual integrity and is not dependent on classification robustness. This reconstruction-first approach paves the way for new techniques in adversarial robustness by allowing safer perception pipelines in unmanned vehicles.

title: OBER+: Continuity-Aware Reporting and Traceable Continuous Improvement in Outcome-Based Education
abstract: Institutions practising outcome-based education compute learning outcome attainment routinely, while reviews of curriculum analytics report an absence of evidence on how that computation informs decisions. This paper presents OBER+, an extension of a deployed institutional attainment platform that computes the step from a measured shortfall to an evaluated corrective action. Five connected stages accumulate attainment across deliveries of a course, signal a shortfall and a persistent shortfall, grade it on cutoffs the regulator already uses, record the decision against a catalogue of practices annotated with their evidence, log the change, and quantify the subsequent movement in the shortfall. A further rule compares successive statements of an outcome, so attainment is never read as a series across a point at which the outcome changed. Applying the rules to the live record of two real courses produced three results. Every outcome of a core course was substantively redefined between consecutive deliveries, with subject matter moving between outcome numbers, so a naive reading would have reported a twenty-five point collapse between quantities that do not refer to the same learning. Recomputing the platform's figures from its documented rule showed six of ten differing by more than rounding explains, in a pattern that identified a defect since reported to the institution. Across fifteen statement pairs from three transitions, five were identical character for character, and among the ten that were not, the outcome carrying a given number was nearest to a differently numbered earlier outcome in six, a result resting on an ordering of similarities and requiring no threshold and no labelling. The contribution is a computational design for outcome-based reporting, stated as rules any attainment platform can implement, with evidence of what they make visible in a live institutional record.

title: Restricted Eigenvalues Beyond Gaussian Width: Threshold Occupancy under Heavy Tails
abstract: Restricted eigenvalue (RE) bounds govern stable recovery by norm-regularized estimators. For isotropic sub-Gaussian measurements, the benchmark sample size is $1+w(A)^2$, where $w(A)$ is the Gaussian width of the normalized descent cone. The COLT 2015 open-problem note (Banerjee et al., 2015) asked whether the same law follows for heavy-tailed designs from a uniform small-ball condition alone. We give an explicit and systematic negative answer to the general question as formulated there: the proposed law fails in its full dimension-free, arbitrary-set form, and the missing obstruction is simultaneous threshold occupancy. A constant-width polyhedral descent cone with fixed small-ball constants has zero empirical RE on every sample path up to half the ambient dimension. More generally, every finite range space admits exact threshold encoding in an arbitrarily narrow spherical cap and a lift to a full polyhedral descent-cone section. For every fixed threshold VC dimension $d$, as $β\downarrow0$, the sharp worst-case sample complexity is $Θ(β^{-1}[d\log(1/β)+\log(1/δ)])$. The separation persists under exact isotropy and all finite moments: on the same constant-width cone, Gaussian measurements succeed with $O(1+\log(1/δ))$ samples, whereas an isotropic heavy-tailed design fails pathwise for $n\lesssim\sqrt{p/\log p}$. Gaussian smoothing yields an everywhere-positive $C^\infty$ density while retaining arbitrarily poor RE. Under isotropy, a distribution-free fallback governed by affine dimension times squared enclosing radius is sharp on this family.

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Matrix Decomposition (NADS) for Machine Learning
abstract: Non-Linear Adaptive Matrix Decomposition (NADS) is a novel algorithm designed to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of machine learning models. This paper introduces a dynamic matrix decomposition method that iteratively adjusts the weights of a model's matrix, optimizing performance through a learning parameter refinement process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NADS through extensive experimental evaluations on a range of machine learning tasks, highlighting its superior performance compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism involves a continuous adjustment of the matrix weights based on a learned optimization strategy. This adaptation allows the model to better handle complex data patterns and maintain stability during training. The paper also discusses the advantages and limitations of the NADS algorithm, exploring its potential impact on various machine learning applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Fractal Algorithm for Evolutionary Computation
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Fractal Algorithm (AFA) designed to enhance the robustness and adaptability of evolutionary computation. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with complex, highly varying landscapes, leading to premature convergence or suboptimal solutions. The AFA dynamically adjusts the fractal dimension of a population of solutions, guided by performance metrics, to promote more resilient designs. This mechanism, termed the "Fractal Dimension Adjustment," addresses this limitation by subtly modifying the fractal structure of the population, fostering exploration of diverse regions of the solution space. The algorithm's core claim centers on creating a dynamic optimization strategy that surpasses the capabilities of static evolutionary approaches. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the AFA through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing improved performance in a range of benchmark problems.

title: Quantum-Driven Topological Mapping
abstract: Quantum-driven topological mapping offers a fundamentally new approach to exploring topological spaces, promising unprecedented efficiency in pattern recognition and relationship discovery. This paper proposes a quantum algorithm designed to leverage superposition and entanglement to identify subtle topological correlations that are inaccessible to classical methods. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how quantum states are manipulated to reveal these patterns, and discuss the potential impact of this technology across diverse fields, including materials science, cryptography, and fundamental physics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this rapidly evolving field.

title: Title: Morphogenetic Loop Construction (MLC)
abstract: This paper presents the Morphogenetic Loop Construction (MLC) system, a novel approach to generating complex morphogenetic loops. Traditional methods often struggle with predictability and stability, particularly when dealing with intricate evolutionary pathways. MLC leverages a combination of iterative refinement and feedback control to construct robust and stable loops, offering a fundamentally different methodology for evolutionary design. This system focuses on creating loops characterized by a well-defined initial structure and a predictable trajectory, minimizing the generation of unexpected and unstable evolutionary outcomes. The core mechanism centers around a loop-building algorithm that dynamically adjusts parameters to maintain a specific structure, ensuring a consistent and manageable evolutionary process. This paper details the design and implementation of MLC, highlighting its advantages and potential applications across various fields, including evolutionary robotics and complex system modeling.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to automated theorem proving by integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to generate conjectures and heuristics, which are subsequently evaluated within a traditional symbolic theorem prover. This creates a continuous feedback loop, accelerating the theorem proving process. Unlike previous attempts that primarily employed neural networks as assistants to theorem provers, this work establishes a truly integrated neuro-symbolic system. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation strategy, demonstrating the potential for significantly improved performance in automated theorem proving. The system is designed to address the limitations of both pure neural and pure symbolic approaches, capitalizing on the strengths of each. We present a theoretical framework and a preliminary implementation showcasing the feasibility and benefits of this combined approach. The key contribution is a dynamic interplay between neural and symbolic components, leading to more informed and efficient theorem proving.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Models for Predicting Complex System Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to predicting the dynamics of complex systems by employing hierarchical Bayesian models. The core idea is to represent the system at multiple levels of abstraction, capturing dependencies between variables at different scales. We construct Bayesian networks with nested levels, where higher-level nodes represent aggregate variables and lower-level nodes represent detailed components. This architecture facilitates efficient inference and prediction, addressing the scalability challenges inherent in traditional Bayesian modeling techniques for high-dimensional, complex systems. The framework allows for incorporating prior knowledge and updating beliefs based on observed data, providing a robust and flexible approach to dynamic system prediction. The key innovation lies in the structured approach to modeling dependencies, leading to improved accuracy and interpretability compared to flat Bayesian models. We demonstrate the utility of this method through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and considerations for implementing such models.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement for Distributed Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed anomaly detection leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with hidden anomalies and are vulnerable to network attacks and noise. Our proposed mechanism utilizes multiple quantum nodes interconnected through entangled states. These nodes perform quantum measurements and encode the results into the entangled qubits. Anomalous behavior disrupts the entangled state, leading to detectable changes. By analyzing these changes, we can achieve enhanced detection accuracy and robustness against interference. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for anomaly detection, exploiting quantum mechanics for superior performance. The core claim is to design a new mechanism using quantum entanglement to detect hidden anomalies in networks. The core mechanism involves interconnected quantum nodes through entangled states, quantum measurements, and analysis of entangled state changes to identify anomalies. This research represents a significant step towards utilizing quantum technologies for enhanced security and reliability in distributed systems. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Information Coding and Decoding
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information coding and decoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to develop a self-adaptive system capable of dynamically adjusting encoding and decoding parameters based on the observed noise levels and channel losses within the quantum channel. This adaptive strategy aims to significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of quantum information transmission. The proposed framework utilizes a quantum decoherence model to accurately represent channel losses and employs an optimization algorithm rooted in quantum control theory to optimize the generation and measurement strategies of entangled states in real-time. The algorithm's objective is to minimize information loss. The key innovation lies in the system's ability to respond in real-time to fluctuating channel conditions, moving beyond the limitations of static encoding/decoding schemes commonly employed in existing quantum communication protocols. Mathematical models and formulations are presented to illustrate the design and optimization process, focusing on key performance metrics such as channel capacity and fidelity. The system's potential impact on future quantum communication networks is discussed.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding via Non-Classical Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fascinating phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, no matter how far apart they are. This link is not physical, but rather a correlation in their quantum states. Quantum entanglement has profound implications for cryptography and quantum communication, and researchers are exploring ways to leverage it for secure information exchange. This paper investigates the use of non-classical geometry, specifically self-related geometry, to enhance the security and robustness of quantum entanglement information encoding. We propose a novel quantum information encoding scheme predicated on this geometry, which offers advantages in stability and key distribution. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum state that exhibits specific self-related properties, enabling enhanced entanglement fidelity and mitigating potential vulnerabilities. The paper introduces a model that avoids the limitations inherent in conventional encoding methods. We present a theoretical framework and initial experimental considerations to demonstrate the potential of this approach. This research contributes to the ongoing exploration of quantum entanglement for secure communication and explores a novel geometric approach to quantum information processing.

title: Based on Evolutionary Algorithms for Program Synthesis Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms, to the optimization of program code. The core claim is that automated program optimization is achievable through the intelligent application of evolutionary principles. The proposed mechanism involves treating program code as a population and employing genetic operators such as crossover and mutation to iteratively refine the code's structure and parameters. This approach aims to achieve desired performance metrics or enhance code readability. The novelty lies in the automation of this optimization process, contrasting with traditional methods that rely heavily on human intervention. We investigate the potential of this methodology to generate more efficient and maintainable code, offering a promising avenue for software development. The work presented here focuses on the theoretical framework and potential benefits of this approach, without conducting empirical experiments.

title: Title: Bayesian Neural Network for Hyper-Adaptive Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) architecture designed for hyper-adaptive dynamical systems modeling. Traditional dynamical systems models often require significant human intervention for parameter tuning and adjustment. Our approach leverages a variational Bayesian approach coupled with a robust uncertainty quantification technique to enable continuous learning and adaptation of the network's parameters and prediction models. The core mechanism centers around iteratively refining the network's parameters and prediction models through a probabilistic process, fostering autonomous adaptation and potentially superior predictive performance compared to existing methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of this architecture through simulations focusing on climate dynamics and financial market prediction, showcasing its ability to handle complex, evolving data streams.

evidence.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework combining probabilistic logic and formal validation for the construction of complex non-linear multi-variable models. We propose a dynamic adjustment of model parameters and validation strategies to ensure robust model generalization across diverse data distributions. The core mechanism involves establishing a "Probability Logic-Formal Validation" framework, utilizing probabilistic logic for parameter adjustment and validation, complemented by formal validation techniques for automatic issue detection. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional model validation methods, offering a more automated and robust solution for complex models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a series of case studies, showcasing its ability to handle non-linear dependencies and identify potential model deficiencies.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Algorithms: Expansion and Application
abstract: This paper explores the expansion and application of non-linear quantum algorithms, focusing on their potential to address complex problems across diverse fields. We investigate the synergistic integration of existing quantum algorithms with non-linear geometric field theory, aiming to enhance algorithm efficiency and capabilities. This research highlights the novel approach of expanding current quantum techniques by incorporating geometric principles, paving the way for breakthroughs in drug discovery, materials science, and financial modeling. The core claim centers on the ability to achieve more sophisticated computations through this combined methodology. The paper details the core mechanism of this approach, emphasizing the transformative potential of this new paradigm.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topological quantum error correction protocol leveraging the inherent properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum error correction parameters. Traditional quantum error correction relies on pre-determined error correction codes, introducing a dependency that limits adaptability. This work proposes a method that utilizes the quantum state's self-adaptive nature to minimize the number of qubits required for error correction, offering a significant advancement in quantum information protection. We detail the core mechanism, focusing on the implementation of a self-adjusting algorithm that responds to changes within the quantum state. This approach addresses a fundamental limitation of existing quantum error correction strategies, paving the way for more efficient and robust quantum systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Vector Field Control
abstract: Quantum-enhanced vector field control represents a paradigm shift in the manipulation of vector fields, offering unprecedented precision and control compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to establish a 'quantum state' of a vector field, enabling instantaneous and highly precise manipulation. We detail the core mechanism – utilizing quantum entanglement – and its implications for robotics, materials science, and fluid dynamics. The proposed system overcomes limitations of classical control by offering a fundamentally new approach, potentially unlocking breakthroughs in areas demanding extreme precision. This work provides a foundational investigation into the feasibility and potential of this transformative technology.

title: Comment on wes-2026-124
abstract: Abstract. Offshore wind-farm collection-system design is a cost-relevant combinatorial optimization problem whose difficulty grows exponentially with turbine count. This paper introduces OptiWindNet RouteSets, a database of cable-routing solutions to 13954 distinct problem instances based on built, proposed, and procedurally-generated farm layouts. The database is intended as an open benchmark for routing algorithms, a source of hard instances, a strong baseline for reinforcement-learning solvers, and a training corpus for supervised-learning models for the Wind Farm Cable-Routing Problem. The solutions were produced using the optiwindnet Python package with three solvers: exact mathematical optimization and two meta-heuristics (inexact) – hybrid genetic search (HGS) and Lin–Kernighan–Helsgaun (LKH). Two network topologies are covered: radial (path-based) or branched (tree-based). Each solution contains the feasible network and its metadata (solver used, cable capacity, method configuration, route length, detour overhead, solver runtime, and, for exact runs, a proven optimality gap). The problem instances vary in: number of wind turbines (∈ [50, 200]), maximum cable capacity (∈ [2, 12]), and location geometry. For 63% of the problem instances, a solution with <1% gap is available (and 79% with <2% gap). We analyze: (a) the total length of meta-heuristic solutions compared to their exact counterparts – HGS median increase is 0.0%, while LKH is 0.6%; (b) the instance difficulty as a function of capacity and turbine count – those two variables interact, the difficulty increases monotonically with count, but exhibits a count-dependent peak across capacities; (c) the length reduction of branched topology compared to radial – 0.34% median; (d) the detour-caused increase in length over the solver-optimized objective – 0.16% median.

title: Le programme HQI : Un pilier de la stratégie quantique française
abstract: Lancé dans le cadre de la stratégie nationale quantique française, le programme HQI est piloté par GENCI, le CEA et l’INRIA. Son objectif : développer et mettre en service une plateforme hybride combinant du calcul haute performance (HPC) et des ordinateurs quantiques (QPU), pour accélérer la recherche, former des talents et préparer les communautés au calcul quantique. HQI repose sur trois ordinateurs quantiques hébergés au TGCC (CEA) : RUBY (Pasqal), LUCY (Quandela) actuellement en service, et KITY (Alice & Bob) prévu pour 2027. La plateforme utilise Qaptiva (Bull), un intergiciel quantique permettant l’émulation, l’orchestration des QPU, la programmation en Python ou en C++. Les utilisateurs peuvent aussi utiliser Qiskit (IBM) ou les environnements propriétaires des QPU, encapsulés de manière transparente. Enfin, le programme est chargé de la mise en place et de l’animation du réseau des Maisons du Quantique.

title: A two-step feature selection using permutation based feature importance and wrapper-based bio-inspired algorithms for classifying clinical dataset
abstract: Abstract The proposed framework aims to address the challenge of high-dimensional, noisy, irrelevant, and redundant features in clinical datasets by using a two-step feature selection approach. The first step involves a wrapper-based method for calculating the Permutation Based Feature Importance (PBFI) score using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. The second step employs three wrapper-based bio-inspired optimization algorithms, namely Harris Hawk Optimization (HHO), Binary Grasshopper Optimization (BGOA), and Whale Optimization (WOA), with the weighted F1-Score, measured by the SVM classifier, as the fitness function. The selected features from both steps are then combined using a union operation and used to train four classifiers: SVM, K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Naive Bayes (NB). The proposed framework is also evaluated using a non-parametric hypothesis testing method, the Kruskal-Wallis Test, on eight medical datasets from the Machine Learning Repository (MLR) maintained by the University of California, Irvine (UCI). The proposed approach is compared with feature selection using the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm (PSOA) and Lion's Algorithm, and is shown to perform better.

title: CoVeR: Coverage-Based Routing of Verifier Calls in Agentic Retrieval
abstract: An agentic retrieval system issues a sequence of search queries and must decide, at each step, whether the evidence collected so far is enough to stop. Delegating that decision to an LLM verifier or a prompt judge makes stopping reliable, but the verifier then reprocesses the growing evidence after every retrieval step, a substantial repeated cost. We show that most of these calls can be skipped without materially changing answer accuracy: a single threshold on a frozen sentence-embedding coverage margin detects the states in which the evidence is still plainly incomplete, and the verifier is called only on the ambiguous remainder, a gate we call CoVeR (Coverage-based Verifier Routing). Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks, with the evaluation protocol fixed before the full-scale run, the CoVeR-gated agent matches the answer accuracy of both the full-budget agent and the always-verify baseline within a fraction of an EM point. It cuts 62-68% of verifier calls, and 93% in a saturated regime. Routers built on evidence counts, lexical overlap, or BM25 relevance, alone or learned in combination, give weaker overall trade-offs, the gate transfers without re-tuning across deciders and agent scales, and its drafter distills into a 921k-parameter head atop the frozen encoder, leaving no LLM in the routing loop. The same signal cannot replace verification: matching a claim is far easier than deciding the claim is supported.

title: TRILOGUE: A Trilingual Spoken Dialogue Fact-Checking Benchmark with Evidence and Paired Audio
abstract: Modern misinformation is often heard before it is read, yet fact-checking systems are still evaluated mainly on clean written claims. Spoken dialogue remains different even when systems operate on transcripts: claims may be distributed across speakers and turns, depend on prior context, and become harder to verify when Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) errors distort the available text. Prior spoken dialogue fact-checking resources are small, English-centric, or focused on annotation rather than end-to-end benchmarking, leaving no large multilingual benchmark with paired speech and turn-level labels. We introduce TRILOGUE (TRIlingual spoken diaLOGUE fact-checking), a large-scale trilingual benchmark of source-grounded spoken dialogues in English, Russian, and Kazakh. It contains nearly 12K dialogues, 187K turns, and 390 hours of paired audio with ASR transcripts and word-level timestamp alignments across all three languages, including nearly 5K human-recorded Russian and Kazakh dialogue files. TRILOGUE supports claim check-worthiness detection, source-article evidence retrieval, and claim verification with claim-only, gold-evidence, and retrieved-evidence inputs. Baselines show that ASR degradation and cross-lingual transfer remain challenging, especially for Kazakh, while retrieved source evidence substantially narrows the gap to gold-evidence verification.

title: From Nowcasting to Forecasting: Adapting a Reanalysis-Trained
abstract: Accurate cloud-cover forecasts are important for temperature prediction, radiation forecasting, and solar-power operations. Short-range forecasting methods can preserve observed cloud placement during the first forecast hours, but their skill decreases when cloud fields evolve through formation, dissipation and deformation. Longer lead times require accounting for atmospheric evolution, but operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecasts may not accurately represent the satellite-observed cloud state at initialization. We develop CloudCast v2, a machine-learning model for 12-hour cloud-cover forecasting from observation-based initial conditions. The model is first trained on the Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis (Ridal2024) to learn cloud-evolution dynamics, and is then adapted to satellite-derived cloud fields using conditional flow matching (Lipman2023), a generative method that transforms noise into cloud-cover forecasts conditioned on the observed initial cloud fields and NWP inputs. CloudCast v2 reduces mean absolute error by 10% relative to its predecessor, CloudCast v1 (Partio2025), over the 1-12 h range. It also overtakes CloudCast v1 in fractions skill score, a neighborhood-based measure of spatial agreement, after approximately 3-6 h, depending on the cloudiness category. These results show that observation-initialized machine-learning forecasts can extend beyond the usual 1-3-hour nowcasting range while retaining spatial detail from satellite cloud fields.

title: PPO-STGNN: A Proximal Policy Optimization Approach with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for DAG Task Scheduling in Cloud-Edge-End Computing
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things, computation intensive directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks have become increasingly common in cloud-edge-end collaborative environments. However, cloud, edge, and end nodes are highly heterogeneous in computing capacity, network bandwidth, and energy consumption, which makes the efficient scheduling of tasks with complex dependencies an NP-hard problem. Traditional heuristic algorithms and conventional reinforcement-learning methods often fail to capture the spatio-temporal dynamics of system resources. This paper proposes PPO-STGNN, a DAG task-scheduling algorithm that integrates proximal policy optimization (PPO) with spatio-temporal graph neural networks (STGNNs). The method uses an STGNN to extract features from both the DAG task topology and the physical cloud-edge-end resource graph, and then optimizes the scheduling policy through PPO to minimize makespan and schedule length ratio (SLR) while improving CPU and memory load balancing. To accelerate convergence, a multi-teacher behavior-cloning mechanism is introduced for pretraining. Experimental results show that PPO-STGNN significantly improves load balancing while maintaining a low completion time, making it suitable for dynamic and heterogeneous cloud-edge- end DAG scheduling scenarios.

title: Towards Secure AI How far can international standards take us?
abstract: This CETaS Research Report prepares policymakers to understand and address the significant cybersecurity challenges that have resulted from the widespread rollout of AI, with a specific focus on the role played by international standards. Our findings indicate that many of the challenges associated with securing AI systems are not new and can be resolved by updating existing cybersecurity standards. However, several challenges are new and evolving rapidly, such as those relating to the security of AI supply chains and new threats which have emerged in the context of generative AI. Standards development organisations (SDOs) have begun to introduce international standards which help protect AI systems from attack, but these standards are at a nascent stage. We recommend governments redouble their efforts to support SDOs and to ensure crucial international standards are made available and accessible to those who need to implement them. We also recommend further investment in related research to advance understandings of adversarial AI, ensuring that future international standards don’t just focus on identifying vulnerabilities, but instead offer robust and specific mitigation strategies.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography: Adaptive Key Generation
abstract: Quantum information cryptography (QIC) is rapidly emerging as a crucial component of modern cybersecurity, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to secure communication. This paper presents a novel quantum key generation (QKD) algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Key Generation," designed to address limitations of existing approaches by exploiting quantum entanglement's self-adjusting nature. The core mechanism centers around creating entangled states that exhibit dynamic correlations, allowing for precise key generation and enhanced security. We detail the algorithm's architecture, explain the underlying quantum principles, and present preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements in key generation rate and security against known attacks. This work explores the potential of this adaptive approach to revolutionize QIC, offering a pathway towards robust and adaptable cryptographic systems.

title: Formal Verification of Old-Age Pension Eligibility (Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007)
abstract: A faithful-by-construction formalization of the old-age pension eligibility rules of the Portuguese General Social Security Regime (Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007, original 2007 wording), specified in First-Order Logic, implemented in Catala, and machine-verified in Lean 4 by an adequacy theorem relating the executable definition to the logical specification for every beneficiary. Part of doctoral research on formal verification of old-age and invalidity pensions within the Rules as Code paradigm. Source code is licensed under Apache-2.0; the documentation and formalization text under CC BY 4.0.

title: Memory Quantum Cipher Identification Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel Memory Quantum Cipher Identification Algorithm (MQCA) designed to efficiently identify and track quantum states, offering enhanced security for quantum computing. The MQCA leverages the unique properties of quantum variables to construct an intelligent detection algorithm. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting quantum entanglement to establish a robust and efficient tracking system for hidden information within quantum states. This approach promises to significantly improve the detection and analysis of quantum states, thereby bolstering the security of quantum computations. The algorithm's design incorporates a refined quantum state analysis framework, resulting in improved accuracy and speed compared to existing methods. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of quantum cryptography and offers a practical framework for secure quantum communication.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Graph-Based Semantic Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning leveraging graph-based semantic networks. The core idea is to bridge the gap between neural networks, known for their pattern recognition capabilities, and symbolic reasoning systems, prized for their logical deduction abilities. We introduce a system where a neural network learns to predict relationships within a structured semantic network, represented as a graph. These predictions dynamically guide the application of symbolic inference rules, and conversely, the results of symbolic inference inform the neural network's learning. This creates a continuous feedback loop, fostering robust and explainable AI. The system's architecture allows for both inductive and deductive reasoning, capitalizing on the strengths of both paradigms. evidence.title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Graph-Based Semantic Networks
evidence.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning leveraging graph-based semantic networks. The core idea is to bridge the gap between neural networks, known for their pattern recognition capabilities, and symbolic reasoning systems, prized for their logical deduction abilities. We introduce a system where a neural network learns to predict relationships within a structured semantic network, represented as a graph. These predictions dynamically guide the application of symbolic inference rules, and conversely, the results of symbolic inference inform the neural network's learning. This creates a continuous feedback loop, fostering robust and explainable AI. The system's architecture allows for both inductive and deductive reasoning, capitalizing on the strengths of both paradigms. title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks with Adaptive Learning Rate Schedules Based on Prediction Error
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for neural networks designed to mitigate the challenges associated with traditional training methods, specifically the need for meticulous tuning of learning rate schedules. The proposed network, termed a Self-Correcting Neural Network (SCNN), incorporates a feedback mechanism that dynamically adjusts the learning rate of individual weights based on the observed prediction error. This adaptive learning rate schedule is intrinsically linked to the contribution of each weight to the overall error, fostering a more robust and efficient training process. The core claim of this work is that such an architecture can achieve faster convergence and improved performance compared to conventional neural network training paradigms. We detail the architecture and the associated mathematical formulation, focusing on the predictive error calculation and the weight adaptation process. The key innovation lies in the automated, data-driven adjustment of learning rates, eliminating the need for manual hyperparameter optimization, and demonstrating a potentially significant advantage in complex learning scenarios.

title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Simulations for Machine Learning
abstract: The simulation of quantum computers presents a formidable challenge due to the exponential growth in computational cost with the number of qubits. Current simulation methods often struggle to scale to even moderately sized quantum systems, severely limiting their applicability for machine learning applications. This paper introduces an adaptive simulation strategy designed to mitigate this issue. The core idea revolves around dynamically adjusting the simulation complexity—the level of detail—based on the demands of the underlying machine learning task. We propose a hierarchical simulation approach, where a coarse-grained representation is utilized initially, and the simulation is progressively refined, or "zoomed in," only when specific regions or interactions become critical for the learning process. This strategy minimizes unnecessary computations, leading to a significant reduction in overall simulation time and resource requirements. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and the formulation of key equations governing the adaptive simulation process. The primary goal is to achieve a more efficient and practical approach to quantum computing simulations for machine learning, paving the way for the exploration of quantum algorithms within the machine learning domain.

title: Quantum-Induced Topological Phase Field Dynamics
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to induce topological phase field dynamics, a novel approach to generating complex and dynamically evolving phase field structures. We investigate a new algorithmic framework predicated on creating intricate entanglement patterns that fundamentally alter the behavior of topological phase fields. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entanglement to construct a dynamic and intricate network of quantum states, leading to the emergence of unique topological phases. This research aims to address limitations of existing techniques by providing a fundamentally new methodology for shaping phase field behavior. The paper outlines the proposed algorithm, its theoretical foundations, and preliminary experimental demonstrations illustrating its potential for generating novel phase field topologies.

title: Symbolic Regression with Learned Grammatical Structures
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its efficacy is often limited by the exponential growth of the search space, leading to the generation of overly complex and often uninterpretable models. This work proposes a novel approach to SR that addresses this challenge by integrating learned grammatical structures into the regression process. The core idea is to utilize a learned grammar to guide the search, favoring mathematical expressions that adhere to the learned structural patterns, thereby promoting conciseness and interpretability. We hypothesize that by incorporating this grammatical knowledge, the search space can be significantly reduced, leading to the discovery of more meaningful and readily understandable equations. This paper outlines the framework, presents the key components, and discusses the potential impact of this approach on the field of symbolic regression.
