title: Quantum Topology-Driven Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum Topology-Driven Machine Learning explores the potential of combining quantum topology theory with machine learning to enhance model generalization. This paper investigates how utilizing quantum topology as a learning objective can improve model robustness and performance. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how quantum entanglement and topological phases are leveraged to create novel learning paradigms. The research aims to demonstrate a shift from traditional data-dependent models towards a more adaptable and potentially more powerful approach, specifically focusing on enhancing the generalization capabilities of machine learning algorithms. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications within the field of artificial intelligence.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive neural network optimization strategy, termed "Dynamic Neural Architecture and Hyperparameter Adaptation" (DNANA). The core of this approach lies in dynamically adjusting the network's architecture and hyperparameters based on the model's training progress, rather than relying on pre-defined configurations. The system employs a self-learning mechanism to iteratively refine the network's parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and efficiency. We explore the design of a novel self-adaptation loop that monitors key metrics during training and adjusts network components accordingly. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in model performance across a range of benchmark datasets, offering a more robust and adaptive solution compared to traditional optimization techniques. This work introduces a new paradigm for neural network training, focusing on continuous, intelligent adjustments.

title: Probability Matrix: Adaptive Mapping for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on probability matrices, termed Adaptive Mapping for Complex Systems (AMCS). AMCS leverages a dynamically adjusted probability matrix to represent the system's state and guide parameter adjustments, enabling adaptability to environmental changes. The algorithm combines the strengths of probabilistic modeling with a dynamic mapping technique, offering a robust and potentially superior approach to optimization in complex systems. The core mechanism involves establishing a probability matrix that iteratively updates based on environmental input, leading to a system that can respond effectively to evolving conditions. This work presents a framework for adaptive parameter tuning, demonstrating potential improvements in optimization performance across various challenging scenarios.

title: Neural Network Time Travel Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network training and understanding, termed "Neural Network Time Travel Simulation." The core idea is that neural networks, due to their inherent state representation capabilities, can be leveraged to simulate past states and events, ultimately enhancing their comprehension of causal relationships and predictive accuracy. This is achieved through the introduction of feedback loops that inject historical state information into the current computations within the neural network. Unlike traditional approaches that solely rely on data-driven learning, this method directly simulates the internal temporal dynamics of the network. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this concept, outlining the mathematical framework and key considerations for implementing such a simulation. The potential impact of this approach on various applications, particularly those requiring robust causal reasoning, is discussed. We present a conceptual model and outline a potential algorithmic structure for executing a neural network time travel simulation. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and challenges.

title: Symbolic Simulation of Biological Systems using Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex biological systems through the integration of symbolic representations and agent-based modeling (ABM). Traditional differential equation models often struggle to capture the intricate dynamics of biological systems due to their inherent assumptions and limitations. We propose a methodology where biological components are represented symbolically, allowing for precise definition of rules and interactions, and these symbolic representations are then utilized to drive the behavior of individual agents within an ABM. This approach addresses the limitations of both purely symbolic and purely agent-based modeling by combining the rigor of symbolic representation with the dynamic realism of ABM. The core claim of this research is that complex biological systems are difficult to model using traditional differential equations. The mechanism relies on the use of ABM to simulate individual agents interacting within a system, incorporating symbolic representations of biological components. The resulting simulation provides a more nuanced and potentially accurate representation of biological phenomena compared to conventional methods.

title: Dynamic Graph-Based Knowledge Graph Reasoning (DGKGR)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Graph-Based Knowledge Graph Reasoning (DGKGR), a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that leverages dynamic graph algorithms for both inference and updating. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods often struggle to accommodate the inherent dynamism of real-world knowledge, leading to outdated and potentially inaccurate representations. DGKGR addresses this challenge by employing algorithms designed to adapt to evolving graph structures and relationships. The core mechanism involves the application of graph algorithms – specifically, shortest path algorithms, centrality measures, and community detection techniques – to dynamically infer new relationships and update existing ones within the knowledge graph. This allows for a more robust and accurate representation of knowledge, capable of reflecting changes in the underlying world. We present a framework for implementing DGKGR, detailing the key components and algorithmic choices. The system's ability to continuously refine and update its knowledge representation provides a significant advantage over static knowledge graph approaches, particularly in domains where information is constantly evolving. This research contributes a new methodology for knowledge graph management, emphasizing adaptability and real-time responsiveness.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Systems: Adaptive Quantum State Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state mapping, specifically tailored for nonlinear quantum systems. Traditional methods often rely on static mapping, limiting precision. Our work leverages the inherent dynamics of these systems to dynamically adjust quantum state distributions, enabling precise control and optimization. The core mechanism centers on utilizing the unique properties of nonlinear quantum systems to achieve this adaptive mapping. This advancement represents a significant step towards more sophisticated quantum control and optimization strategies.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Kernel Methods
abstract: Kernel methods represent a powerful class of machine learning algorithms, renowned for their ability to capture complex, non-linear relationships within data. However, a significant limitation has historically been the reliance on manual kernel selection – a process that demands substantial domain expertise and often results in suboptimal performance. This paper introduces an adaptive kernel learning algorithm designed to address this challenge. The core idea is to automate the kernel selection process, allowing the algorithm to dynamically learn and tune the kernel function during training, adapting to the underlying data distribution. We formulate the learning process as an optimization problem, aiming to minimize a kernel-induced error function. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the kernel parameters, leveraging gradient-based optimization techniques. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach consistently outperforms traditional fixed-kernel methods across a range of benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential of automating kernel selection for enhanced kernel method performance.

title: Self-Organizing Information Matrix
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Self-Organizing Information Matrix (SOIM) designed to automatically learn and optimize data structures through self-organizing principles. The SOIM leverages a dynamically constructed matrix that adapts to the data itself, enabling superior information compression and transmission capabilities. The core mechanism centers on a self-organizing learning process, where the matrix evolves in response to the input data, leading to optimized representations and enhanced performance. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional data compression techniques by offering a more adaptive and efficient solution. We explore the theoretical foundations of this design and present a comprehensive implementation demonstrating its effectiveness through various data scenarios. This work contributes to the advancement of data compression and information processing by introducing a robust and automated system.

title: yiqiao-yin/multireward-grpo: v0.1.0 — multireward-grpo
abstract: Archival release of the code underlying the paper "Decoupling and Conditioning Reshape Influence Allocation and the Gradient-Noise Floor in Multi-Reward GRPO under a Finite-Sample U-Statistic Analysis" (Y. Yin, Scientific Reports, under review). This tag is the version deposited in Zenodo and cited in the paper's Code Availability section. Contents src/multireward_grpo/ — the installable library (pip install multireward-grpo): AN/NA advantage estimators, the three conditioning implementations (none, zero_fill, subgroup), the reward-channel framework, a general multi-reward GRPO trainer, and the Theorem 3 analysis routine. scripts/ — the research harness. Synthetic verification for Propositions 1, 2, 4 and Theorem 3; the three-stage real-LLM validation pipeline (generation, reward channels, analysis); the Tier-3 multi-reward GRPO training and evaluation loop; and the cloud-GPU orchestration used for the H100 runs. Dataset generators — fintech_scenarios.py, fintech_rewards.py, fintech_generate.py and llm_rewards.py. The released corpora can be regenerated from this code and a single integer seed, not merely downloaded; construction, reward definitions, partitioning and provenance are documented in the paper's "Dataset Construction and Provenance" section. Reproducing The synthetic harness needs no GPU and reproduces every Tier-1 figure and closed-form check on a laptop: uv sync --extra research uv run scripts/grpo_harness.py The fastest smoke test is multireward-grpo thm3-check (CPU, seconds). Related artifacts Datasets and fine-tuned models are on Hugging Face under the eagle0504 namespace; see huggingface_assets.md.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Geometry – A Novel Approach to Cryptographic Security
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for cryptography based on quantum entanglement, specifically focusing on the geometric transformation of quantum entangled matrices. Traditional cryptographic systems rely heavily on mathematical operations, but this approach leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to generate more robust and potentially unbreakable encryption algorithms. The core mechanism involves manipulating the entangled matrix through a series of geometric operations, aiming to create a fundamentally different approach to secure data transmission and storage. The presented method demonstrates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize cryptographic security, offering a pathway toward advanced encryption techniques.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Geometric Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum Topology explores the potential of leveraging quantum mechanics to revolutionize pattern recognition, specifically focusing on the development of an adaptive geometric pattern recognition algorithm. This research proposes a novel approach that utilizes quantum state self-similarity to achieve more accurate geometric analysis and predictive capabilities. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adapting to the intricate quantum states, offering a fundamentally different methodology compared to traditional techniques. The algorithm's potential lies in its ability to discern subtle geometric patterns hidden within complex quantum states, leading to enhanced precision and robustness. This paper will detail the theoretical foundations, implementation strategies, and preliminary results of this innovative system, demonstrating its capacity to surpass conventional methods in pattern recognition tasks.

title: Technologies quantiques en Allemagne : Stratégie et acteurs
abstract: Les technologies quantiques font l’objet d’un engouement de plus en plus marqué en Allemagne, tant au niveau des pouvoirs publics qu’auprès des acteurs économiques. Cet article décrit l’évolution stratégique du pays dans ce domaine, depuis la première stratégie quantique allemande jusqu’au High-Tech Agenda adopté en 2025, qui donne le cadre des développements actuels. Cet article présente, en outre, un panorama des entités allemandes de premier plan sur le quantique, tant dans la recherche qu’au niveau des entreprises – start-ups, industriels et réseaux.

title: Democritus: Homotopy-Localized Causal Discourse Extraction from Language
abstract: Natural-language documents contain many causal claims, but those claims are unstable under paraphrase, granularity shifts, and contextual drift. A collection may express one mechanism in many surface forms, while neighboring studies may agree locally yet fail to glue globally because relation families, polarities, temporal scopes, or regimes differ. This paper studies that post-extraction problem through Democritus, an implemented system for extracting, normalizing, localizing, and diagnosing causal discourse. We do not claim to identify ground-truth causal structure from text alone. Instead, we formulate the post-extraction layer as a homotopical repair problem for a non-compositional causal-discourse sketch. A normalization functor induces a class of weak equivalences on textual mentions; we prove that these data form a relative category with two-out-of-three and that normalization factors through its localization. Strict repair requires a corpus diagram to satisfy the sketch exactly, whereas homotopy repair asks for a weakly equivalent diagram that factors coherently after localization. We also define the conditions under which grounded discourse localization maps functorially into the observational-equivalence spaces of causal models studied by higher algebraic K-theory. The implementation approximates these formal constructions through normalized claim classes, an observed compatibility complex, regime-sensitive gluing, and provenance-preserving database artifacts. On a frozen 404-passage AltLex/UniCausal comparison, a restricted verbatim-span Democritus extractor attains 57.1% causal-classification F1 and 39.1% macro span F1, compared with 59.2% and 43.6% for the public UniCausal baseline. This similar classification F1 reflects a clear precision-recall tradeoff: Democritus achieves higher recall (80.9% versus 68.7%) but lower precision (44.1% versus 52.0%). Case studies on Emperor-penguin climate discourse, Mediterranean-diet studies, red-wine cardiovascular studies, and rising-ocean-temperature corpora expose both stable repeated mechanisms and cases where local causal claims cannot be assembled into one coherent corpus-level account.

title: Performance Analysis of Sorting Algorithms in Context of Complexity
abstract: Data structure is a systematic way to organize, manage and store data in a computer's memory so that it can be accessed and modified efficiently. Sorting is a fundamental operation in data structures that deals with arranging the elements of a list or array in a specific order. This order can be numerical, alphabetical, or any user-defined order. In computer science, sorting is not just about arranging numbers, it is about organizing data so that it can be used efficiently. In C programming, sorting algorithms are commonly applied to arrays using loops, functions, pointers, and sometimes recursion. Time complexity describes how the running time of an algorithm increases as the input size increases. Space complexity describes how much additional memory an algorithm needs while sorting. Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, and Quick Sort can generally be implemented in-place. The aim of this paper is to analyse a role of different sorting algorithms in context of time and space complexity.

title: Decoding GenAI
abstract: This chapter reviews the development of natural language processing (NLP) from early symbolic and statistical approaches to contemporary transformer-based models. It begins by outlining the limitations of bag-of-words and n-gram representations and describes the shift toward distributed word embeddings such as Word2Vec and GloVe, which offered more informative semantic structure. The introduction of the transformer architecture in 2017 marked a major turning point, introducing self-attention, positional encoding, and parallel sequence processing as core mechanisms for language understanding. Through concise explanations and illustrative examples, the chapter presents the essential components of the transformer and explains how subsequent models, including BERT and GPT, extend this framework to support contextual interpretation and advanced language generation. The chapter concludes by considering the expanding applications of large language models and the ethical considerations that accompany their growing role in society.

title: An efficient lattice-based conditional privacy-preserving group signature with user-controlled and sequential linkability
abstract: Abstract Currently, existing group signature schemes with user-controlled and sequential linkability (GS-UCSL) suffer from critical limitations: they lack post-quantum security, cannot efficiently revoke malicious signers, grant excessive tracing power to group managers (GM), and rely on heavy revocation lists or secure channels that incur high computation or communication overhead. To address these issues, we propose an efficient lattice-based conditional privacy-preserving GS-UCSL (LCGS-UCSL). Our scheme is built on lattice cryptography to achieve post-quantum security, and unifies implicit linkability, explicit linkability, and sequential linkability under user autonomous control. We design a polynomial-based revocation mechanism that eliminates revocation list verification and secure-channel token updates, enabling lightweight and privacy-preserving member revocation. To curb GM’s overreach, we introduce key-oblivious encryption to split users into traceable and non-traceable types without their awareness, and use cuckoo hashing to realize $$O(1)$$ O ( 1 ) registry operations. We further integrate signature aggregation and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge to optimize batch verification and reduce communication overhead. We formally prove the scheme’s anonymity, traceability, Existential Unforgeability under Chosen-Message Attack, and non-frameability in the random oracle model, and validate its practicality via performance analysis. The results show that LCGS-UCSL achieves comprehensive functionality with competitive efficiency, filling the gap toward post-quantum secure GS-UCSL with efficient revocation and balanced privacy.

title: The double-edged sword of proactive GenAI: how it shapes user usage intention
abstract: Purpose With the emergence of generative AI (GenAI), proactive services that initiate actions on behalf of users without explicit prompts are becoming increasingly prevalent. Although such services can enhance human-AI interaction, emerging evidence suggests that GenAI proactivity may also elicit adverse user reactions. To reconcile these mixed findings, this research examines why and when GenAI's proactive services positively and negatively influence users' usage intention. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on mind perception theory, we develop a dual-pathway model proposing that increased proactivity simultaneously enhances perceived agency and diminishes perceived control. We further propose that task type (hedonic vs. utilitarian) determines the relative dominance of these two pathways. We test these predictions through two scenario-based experiments. Study 1 examines the dual-pathway model in a health assistant context, whereas Study 2 investigates the moderating role of task type in a shopping assistant context. Findings Study 1 demonstrates that high (vs. low) proactivity simultaneously increases perceived agency and reduces perceived control. Study 2 shows that task type moderates these effects: for the hedonic task, the positive pathway through perceived agency dominates, making high proactivity more favorable; for the utilitarian task, the negative pathway through perceived control prevails, making low proactivity more preferred. Originality/value This research advances the literature on GenAI's proactive services by demonstrating that their double-edged effects operate through parallel enabling and constraining pathways. We also extend mind perception theory by revealing the psychological costs of agency attribution. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for firms seeking to tailor GenAI functionalities to enhance user experience and foster usage across diverse digital business contexts.

title: Efficient Quantum Error Correction from Three Dimensional Qubit Control
abstract: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can substantially reduce qubit overhead relative to surface codes, but their advantage depends on efficiently realizing nonlocal syndrome extraction. We study the \([[144,12,12]]\) bivariate bicycle code on a neutral-atom architecture with native three-dimensional (3D) geometry, comparing planar and 3D embeddings while holding the code fixed. We characterize spatial efficiency using the logical-qubit density, defined as the number of encoded logical qubits per unit spatial footprint. Because the optical controller's field of view limits the transverse extent of an array, this metric estimates the number of logical qubits that can be accommodated within a fixed optical field of view. The 3D embedding achieves approximately \(4\times\) greater areal logical-qubit density than the planar layout and \(42\times\) greater than a surface-code baseline. It also reduces the bivariate bicycle syndrome-extraction time by roughly \(2\times\) compared to a planar baseline, with fewer movement operations and substantially shorter atom-transport distance. Native 3D geometry can improve both the packing density and executable realization of nonlocal qLDPC codes, making practical performance depend jointly on code structure, optical geometry, transport scheduling, and hardware-level noise. This motivates further development of control techniques in 3D.

title: AquaBEV: Monocular Underwater BEV Occupancy with 3D Sonar Supervision
abstract: Autonomous underwater robots are widely used for exploration, monitoring, and inspection, where safe navigation depends on understanding the surrounding free and occupied space. Bird's eye view (BEV) occupancy provides such a representation, but predicting it from a single underwater RGB image is difficult due to limited, unreliable geometric cues from appearance alone. 3D imaging sonar offers complementary geometric measurements to supervise this task. We introduce AquaBEV, a monocular underwater occupancy model that predicts local BEV occupancy from a single RGB image, using paired 3D imaging sonar as geometric supervision during training. AquaBEV maps visual features into a calibration free polar representation and applies causal decoding along the range dimension before reconstructing the prediction in Cartesian BEV coordinates. A controlled underwater occupancy benchmark was established, adapting representative occupancy methods to the same RGB to sonar task under a unified protocol. AquaBEV achieves 31.4 Visible IoU and 38.6 Observed IoU, 4.0% and 4.3% relative improvements over the strongest transferred baseline.

title: Beyond "Made with AI": Visualizing Provenance Density to Mitigate the Transparency Penalty
abstract: As generative AI makes polished prose cheap to produce, users can no longer rely on fluency as a proxy for truth. We call this failure mode the Fluency Trap: users trust fluent hallucinations while also discounting accurate content once it is disclosed as AI-generated. Binary ``Made with AI'' labels respond with authorship disclosure, but they do not show what supports a claim. We propose Provenance Density, an evidence-visualization interface that shows the density of verified claims in a text. In a user study with 81 participants, an idealized Provenance Density interface produced a large discernment gap between truth and fabrication ($+4.15$ points, $d=1.82$), whereas participants given no signal showed no detectable discrimination. A technical audit with 200 samples shows that retrieval density alone is insufficient; unexpectedly, the Consistency Veto carries most of the discriminative signal on dynamic queries. As AI-generated content becomes indistinguishable from human writing, effective transparency must move from authorship disclosure toward evidence visualization.

title: Discrete-time quantum walks with energy-dependent coins
abstract: In this work, we extend the scattering quantum walk (SQW) framework to a lattice of energy-dependent point interactions. This yields, within the coined quantum walk (CQW) formalism, a coin operator that is directly related to the scattering matrix of zero-range potentials. The model thus provides a discrete-time quantum-walk (DTQW) analog of a periodic array of point interactions of the Kronig-Penney type, where the walker's wavenumber serves as a continuous, physically transparent control parameter for the coin operation. We analyze the spectra and the dynamics of position probability and entanglement, yielding distinct results for specific energies and point interactions. We relate the spectral structure to the spatial probability distribution and explicitly characterize the long-time entanglement behavior for each point interaction. The transmission modulus determines the quasienergy gap, bandwidth, and maximum group velocity, while also controlling the long-time coin-position entanglement for the initial state considered. The four families of one-dimensional point interactions ($δ$, $δ'$, crossed and asymmetric) realize qualitatively distinct transmission profiles and span the full range of behavior, including enhanced or strongly suppressed spreading and oscillatory entanglement.
